# Slots: the stages of the pipeline and what can go into each

GraspPanda builds a grasp detector from stages, and every stage is a **slot** of the config: a place where one component can be replaced by another that keeps the same contract. This page is the map: the pipeline, the task of every slot, its 248 options in all, and which option was measured to work under which method. Every slot has a page of its own with one row and one command per option.

**No accuracy is claimed for any option that is not one of the six ported methods.** An option is listed because it was built, trained for 20 iterations on 8 real frames of GraspNet-1Billion and asked to predict (`grasppanda probe`). That shows it is usable, not that it is good; the model zoo is still empty.

To try options without reading further, open the [combination explorer](../explorer/index.md): pick a method, change a slot, read the measured verdict and the command.

## The pipeline

```text
observation: a depth image as a point cloud (HGGD also reads the colour image)
  │
  ├─ the seed-based methods
  │    scene encoder ─► seed proposal ─► view ─► (assigner) ─► grouper ─► head bundle ─┐
  │    features         seeds            approach  labels,       crops                 │
  │                                                training                            │
  └─ HGGD: image encoder ─► heat-map and region stages (no slots of their own yet) ────┤
  grasps for the evaluator or a robot ◄─ post-processing ◄─ GraspGroup ◄───────────────┘

around the model: the loss of every stage · the training recipe
```

Six methods are ported. Five share the seed-based skeleton and therefore its six stage slots (GSNet, EconomicGrasp, FineGrasp, GraspNet-baseline, Scale-Balanced-Grasp); HGGD is a detector family of its own with one slot so far, the image encoder. Losses, post-processing and the training recipe are around the stages and apply to all six.

## The slots

An option is a name you can write after `--set <slot>=`: a preset (a component with settings for table-top depth clouds) or a component with its defaults.

| Slot | Task, and input → output | Options |
|---|---|---|
| **[Image encoder](image_encoders.md)**<br>`model.image_encoder` | Turns the colour (or RGB-D) image into feature maps. HGGD predicts its grasp heat-map from them; a seed-based method can read them at the pixel of every point (point painting).<br>*image `(B, C, H, W)` → a list of feature maps, finest first* | 38 (4 component types) |
| **[Scene encoder](scene_encoders.md)**<br>`model.backbone` | The first learned stage of a seed-based method: one feature vector per point of the depth cloud. Its receptive field is what a seed knows before any crop is taken.<br>*points `(N, 3)` in metres, camera frame, with per-point features → features on every point (`dense`) or on a sub-sample (`subsampled`)* | 47 (29 component types) |
| **[Seed proposal](proposal.md)**<br>`model.proposal` | Decides where grasps are predicted: picks a fixed number of seeds per frame (usually 1024) among the scene points, by a predicted score, a sampler, or both.<br>*encoder features → `SeedSet`: seed points, their features, named scores* | 24 (4 component types; 11 samplers as `model.proposal.sampler`) |
| **[View](view.md)**<br>`model.view` | Chooses the approach direction of every seed: two of the three degrees of freedom of the grasp orientation, and the frame the crop is taken in.<br>*`SeedSet` → `ApproachSet`: a unit direction and a rotation per seed, and the index of the label view* | 21 (8 component types) |
| **Assigner**<br>`model.assigner` | Training only: matches every seed with the grasp labels of the scene point it sits on, in the label set the head is supervised with.<br>*seeds, approach, supervision → matched labels (`dense` grids or `compact` best grasps), optional seed weights* | 4 (3 component types) |
| **[Grouper](grouper.md)**<br>`model.grouper` | Gathers the neighbourhood of every seed in the frame of its approach direction and turns it into the feature the head reads.<br>*points with features, crop centres and frames → one feature per seed, or one per seed and depth bin* | 32 (14 component types) |
| **[Head bundle](head_loss.md)**<br>`model.head` | Predicts the grasp at a seed: in-plane rotation, depth, width and score. Network head, target encoder, loss and decoder share one parameterisation, so they are swapped as a whole.<br>*crop features → loss terms in training; `GraspGroup` (one grasp per seed) at prediction* | 10 (4 component types) |
| **[Loss](head_loss.md)**<br>`model.<stage>.<term>_loss` | One term of the loss of a stage (objectness, graspness, view score, grasp score, angle, depth, width). A stage declares the kind of each term, a loss the kinds it fits.<br>*prediction and target of one term → a weighted scalar* | 20 (18 component types) |
| **[Post-processing](post.md)**<br>`evaluation.variants.<name>` | What happens to predicted grasps before an evaluator or a robot gets them: filters, selection, corrections of pose and width, a change of frame. Steps are chained.<br>*`GraspGroup` of one frame and the observation → `GraspGroup`* | 15 (14 component types) |
| **[Training recipe](recipe.md)**<br>`optimizer`, `scheduler`, `hooks`, `data.train.dataset.transforms` | Everything around the model: how weights are updated, how the learning rate moves, what runs around the loop, how a training sample is perturbed.<br>*parameters and gradients → updates; a training sample → a perturbed sample* | 37 (19 component types) |

The assigner has no page of its own: it goes with the head bundle and the label set ([Heads and losses](head_loss.md), [Data contracts](../advanced_guides/data_flow.md)). The scene encoders have an [overview](scene_encoders.md) and three pages: [point-based networks](scene_encoders_point.md), [sparse-voxel networks and released weights](scene_encoders_sparse.md), [transformers and pretrained 3-D encoders](scene_encoders_transformer.md). The encoders ported before these pages are in [Scene encoders of the model zoo](../model_zoo_backbones.md).

## Which option fits which method

From the [measured records](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md), in the words of that page (980 recorded cells: 770 `runs`, 11 `runs-unstable`, 193 `refused`, 6 `fails`). An option **works** under a method when the combination was built, trained for the probe's iterations and predicted, directly or in the adapter compose inserted. Its class counts the methods it works under, with **one slot replaced at a time**:

- **universal**: it works under all five seed-based methods.
- **most**: it works under three or four of them.
- **some**: it works under two.
- **specific**: it works under exactly one.
- **none**: it works under none of them as it was probed.

*≈n*: under n of those methods the run was `runs-unstable`. † The slot was not probed under the five seed-based methods but under the methods of the second column, so its classes count those: *universal* is all of them, *some* one of two, *most* all but one of three, *none* none. *(defaults)*: the component named by its type and built with its constructor defaults, not a preset; a component that needs an option only a preset supplies does not work that way.

- `target-mask` has no cell of its own: reads observation.masks, which no shipped dataset fills.
- `distribution-focal` has no cell of its own: fits `bins` terms only; probed as the width loss of the head preset `decoupled-grid-bins` (stage cells).

How to read it:

- **A class is not a ranking.** *universal* says that a swap needs nothing else; it says nothing about accuracy.
- **An option that is not universal is usually bound to its neighbours, not to a paper.** A head bundle goes with the assigner and the label set it is supervised with, a grouper with the axes its head reads, a scoring proposal with the stage that owns objectness. Replaced together with what they depend on they run under other methods too: see [Sets of stages](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md#sets-of-stages) and [Several slots at once](../advanced_guides/measured_combinations.md#several-slots-at-once).
- **A refusal comes with the fix.** `grasppanda compose` prints the contract that is violated and the option or preset that satisfies it, before anything is built.
- **A loss or a recipe preset in the column *most*, *some* or *none* did not run everywhere it was put**: the [loss](head_loss.md) and [recipe](recipe.md) pages say where and why (a term of another kind, a detector that reads images, mixed precision).
- **What was not probed is not classified.** Most combinations of two or more options have no record; the explorer shows for any two options what the config check answers, which is a weaker statement than a probe.

## How to try one

```bash
grasppanda compose --list grouper                                # the options of a slot
grasppanda compose gsnet/gsnet_sunet14_g1b-realsense_10e \
    --set grouper=roi-grid -o gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                 # a checked config
grasppanda probe gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                             # 20 iterations on
                                                                 # real frames: runs?
grasppanda train gsnet_roi-grid.yaml                             # the real run
```

- Several `--set` go into one command (`--set backbone=point-transformer-v2 --set grouper=cylinder-vector-attention`, a recorded combination); `compose` inserts the adapter the contracts ask for and says so, or refuses with the conflict and the fix.
- `grasppanda compose --show grouper=roi-grid` prints one preset with what must be re-tuned; `grasppanda components --slot groupers` prints the contracts, sources and optional libraries of every component.
- `grasppanda explore` serves the explorer locally and checks any selection with the `compose` of your installation.
- `probe` needs GraspNet-1Billion and the label assets of the method ([Try a combination](../user_guides/combinations.md) lists the `prepare` commands). An option that is a bridge to a library names the extra to install on its slot page.
